observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a large mirrored wall, sheer white curtains on the left, gray curtains and a wall-mounted air conditioner on the right, and a glossy reflective floor. A single woman in a blue star-decorated top, a flared yellow skirt, and tan high-heeled dance shoes stands in front of the mirror with her arms crossed over her chest; several mirror images of her (side and back views) appear across the wall. The camera is stationary; background elements keep identical positions throughout.
visible_changes: The dancer stays in place (no translation across the room); her body and all mirror images remain at the same horizontal positions, so the motion is in-place rotation/weight-shift, not movement through space.

Her crossed-arm posture is held continuously; the change is in torso and head orientation: she begins more side-on and gradually rotates her upper body and turns her head so that more of her back/side faces the camera while her face becomes more visible in the left mirror image (from profile-away toward frontal).

Her feet change from a spread stance with both heels on the floor to a position where one heel lifts and that foot pivots onto the ball (visible in the central figure and the left mirror image), indicating a slow weight transfer / heel-raise / pivot rather than a step forward.
The yellow skirt shifts and flares slightly with the torso rotation (secondary motion of the same garment), and the legs show small knee/ankle adjustments accompanying the weight shift.
Mirror images move in lockstep with the real dancer (reflections, not separate people).
outside_clip_unknowns: The choreographic name or purpose of the movement (turn, bounce, or heel exercise) and what happens before the first frame and after the last frame are not shown.
Whether the rotation continues to a full turn or reverses is not visible in this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and magnitude of torso rotation are hard to disambiguate because multiple mirror views are present.
Which specific foot is the 'working' foot in the pivot is partly obscured by the mirror geometry.
